nateimhoff.highlights: 40 Under Forty · Award-winning creative work · Built for longevity
nateimhoff.description:
Nathan Imhoff is a co-founder of Stark Social Media Agency and leads creative direction across web, brand, and visual systems. His work focuses on clarity, structure, and execution—turning complex ideas into clean, usable design that holds up over time.

Nathan’s path into design started early through self-taught coding, building his own computers, and hands-on experimentation. That foundation carried into formal training, freelance work, agency roles, and city government, including serving as a Graphic & Web Designer for the City of Santa Clarita on nationally recognized projects.

Good design should reduce friction. For Nathan, layout, hierarchy, and structure are functional decisions with long-term consequences. If a site is difficult to update, confusing to navigate, or fragile to maintain, the design has failed—regardless of how it looks at launch.

His commitment to quality work and community involvement has been recognized with the LA County Sheriff’s Department Star Scroll, and he was selected as one of Santa Clarita’s 40 Under Forty for his dedication to excellence and service.

At Stark, Nathan leads creative with a practical standard: design should make execution easier, not harder. The systems he builds are meant to be understood, maintained, and trusted—by clients and internal teams alike.

Nathan continues to refine his craft through ongoing study and hands-on work, bringing together design, technology, and storytelling to create experiences that are intentional, durable, and built to last.
nateimhoff.focus_intro: Nathan approaches creative work as a system—not decoration. His focus is on building design and web foundations that are clear, intentional, and durable, so teams can grow without constantly rebuilding.
nateimhoff.focus:
Design systems | Create consistent visual and layout systems that scale across platforms without breaking.
Web structure & UX | Design sites that prioritize clarity, hierarchy, and real user behavior—not trends.
Brand execution | Translate brand strategy into usable design assets teams can actually maintain.
Creative problem-solving | Balance aesthetics and constraints to deliver clean, practical solutions.

deannaleigh.highlights: 40 Under Forty · 20+ Years Marketing · London Marathon 2024
deannaleigh.description:
Deanna L. Miller is a co-founder of Stark Social Media Agency and leads strategy across social, content, and digital platforms. Her work focuses on clarity, structure, and building systems that scale — helping organizations communicate with intention instead of noise.

Early in her career, Deanna worked in global sourcing and brand management for high-profile video game clients including Ubisoft and Disney Interactive. That experience shaped her ability to manage complex systems, align creative with business goals, and think beyond individual campaigns.

Social media works best when it’s treated as a system, not a scramble. Deanna brings structure to planning, messaging, and execution so brands show up consistently without chasing trends or reacting in real time.

Her work has been recognized both locally and nationally. Deanna was selected as one of Santa Clarita’s 40 Under Forty for her leadership and impact, and she ran the 2024 London Marathon in support of the Royal Society for Blind Children.

Over more than 20 years in marketing, Deanna has worked with startups, nonprofits, and established brands, helping teams refine their voice, build sustainable content practices, and make decisions that compound over time.

At Stark, Deanna’s role is simple in principle and demanding in practice: remove guesswork, create alignment, and make the work easier to sustain. When the system is clear, the results take care of themselves.
deannaleigh.focus_intro: Deanna brings structure to the messy parts—message clarity, content direction, and decisions that compound. Her work is built to be repeatable, easy to maintain, and aligned with real business goals.
deannaleigh.focus:
Positioning + messaging | Clarify what to say, who it’s for, and why it matters.
Content systems | Build repeatable formats and frameworks teams can sustain.
Campaign direction | Turn priorities into clear themes, hooks, and deliverables.
Execution support | Make the work easier to approve, publish, and improve.
